step1_analysis.description: A fully differential amplifier with an NMOS input pair and PMOS active loads. It serves as a gain stage, likely acting as the transconductor for a mixer or a baseband amplifier in the RF front-end.

paper_reference.title: A Dual-Band RF Front-End for WCDMA and GSM Applications

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the amplifier stage.

sky130_expected.calculation: With Vbias=0.9V, PMOS Vov = 0.48V. Id_pmos = 0.5 * 50u * (5/0.5) * 0.48^2 = 57.6 uA per branch. Total current = 115.2 uA. Power = 115.2uA * 1.8V = 207 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper reports power for the entire front-end. This sub-circuit is a single differential pair, so its power is a small fraction of the total.

sky130_expected.calculation: gm_nmos = 2 * 57.6uA / 0.2V = 0.576 mA/V. ro_nmos = ro_pmos = 1 / (0.1 * 57.6uA) = 173 kOhm. With 100k feedback resistors for self-biasing, Rout = 173k || 173k || 100k = 46.6 kOhm. Gain = gm * Rout = 0.576m * 46.6k = 26.8 V/V = 28.5 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Gain is determined by the intrinsic gain of the SKY130 transistors and the loading effect of the self-biasing feedback resistors.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming ~50 fF of parasitic capacitance at the output nodes (Cgd, Cdb of small W/L devices). fp = 1 / (2 * pi * Rout * C_total) = 1 / (2 * pi * 46.6k * 50f) = 68 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The bandwidth is limited by the high output impedance (46.6 kOhm) and parasitic capacitances. It is lower than the RF operating frequency because this specific block likely operates at baseband or IF.

output_swing.description: Peak-to-peak differential output voltage swing for a 20mVpp differential input.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain = 26.8 V/V. Input = 20 mVpp. Output = 26.8 * 20mV = 536 mVpp.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Verifies the transient large-signal behavior and linearity for small inputs.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC voltage gain, -3dB bandwidth, and transient output swing of the differential amplifier. Uses large feedback resistors for stable self-biasing.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Differential Amplifier Testbench

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u

XM1 N0 LABEL_NET_3 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N0 N3 N7 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N1 N3 N6 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N1 LABEL_NET_4 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}

* Power supplies
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
V6 N6 0 1.8
V7 N7 0 1.8

* Bias
V3 N3 0 0.9

* Self-biasing feedback resistors to set stable DC operating point
R1 N0 LABEL_NET_3 100k
R2 N1 LABEL_NET_4 100k

* AC coupling capacitors
C1 IN_P LABEL_NET_3 10u
C2 IN_N LABEL_NET_4 10u

* Input sources (Differential 1V AC, 20mVpp Tran at 10MHz)
V_IN_P IN_P 0 DC 0 AC 0.5 SIN(0 10m 10Meg)
V_IN_N 0 IN_N DC 0 AC 0.5 SIN(0 10m 10Meg)

* Differential to single-ended converter for easy measurement
E1 out_diff 0 N1 N0 1

.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.control
  * 1. DC Operating Point & Power
  op
  let power = -(i(VVDD) + i(V6) + i(V7)) * 1.8
  print power

  * 2. AC Analysis for Gain and Bandwidth
  ac dec 20 10k 10G
  let gain_db = vdb(out_diff)
  meas ac max_gain MAX gain_db
  let gain_3db = max_gain - 3
  meas ac bw_freq WHEN gain_db = gain_3db FALL=1

  * 3. Transient Analysis for Output Swing
  tran 1n 300n
  meas tran vout_diff_max MAX v(out_diff) from=100n to=300n
  meas tran vout_diff_min MIN v(out_diff) from=100n to=300n
  let swing = vout_diff_max - vout_diff_min
  print swing
  
  quit
.endc
.end
